Original MTD: inspected baseline: Host expression, microbial taxonomy and function, and host-microbiome integration are central to MTD.
MTD Explorer: evaluated implementation: Retains and extends the integrated framework.
Interpretation and scope: Builds on the original MTD framework and established external analytical methods.

Original MTD: inspected baseline: The original publication addresses bulk and single-cell RNA-seq.
MTD Explorer: evaluated implementation: The evaluated workflow and reference application concern bulk RNA-seq.
Interpretation and scope: This study does not establish an expansion to single-cell analysis.

Original MTD: inspected baseline: Separate MTD.sh and MTD_SE.sh entry points provide paired-end and single-end workflows.
MTD Explorer: evaluated implementation: A common entry point resolves the layout and validates mate consistency.
Interpretation and scope: SE/PE support itself is inherited; unified handling and validation are the implementation changes.

Original MTD: inspected baseline: The inspected bulk entry point recognizes SRR accessions and calls prefetch/fasterq-dump.
MTD Explorer: evaluated implementation: Recognizes SRR, ERR and DRR inputs and normalizes single-end/paired-end FASTQ handling.
Interpretation and scope: The reference benchmark used local FASTQs; it is not an accession-download validation experiment.

Original MTD: inspected baseline: fastp preparation and Kraken2 host/non-host classification are part of the workflow.
MTD Explorer: evaluated implementation: Retains these tools with explicit settings, validation and coordinated output handling.
Interpretation and scope: Read filtering and host partitioning use the established fastp and Kraken2 methods.

Original MTD: inspected baseline: HISAT2, optional Magic-BLAST and featureCounts are available.
MTD Explorer: evaluated implementation: Retains the engines and coordinates layout-aware alignment/counting.
Interpretation and scope: Magic-BLAST was used in this benchmark; HISAT2 availability is not evidence of a measured HISAT2 run.

Original MTD: inspected baseline: Kraken2 and Bracken generate taxonomic profiles.
MTD Explorer: evaluated implementation: Retains classification and abundance estimation with coordinated matrices and descriptive outputs.
Interpretation and scope: Uses the established Kraken2 and Bracken methods; comparative classification accuracy was not evaluated.

Original MTD: inspected baseline: HUMAnN and MetaPhlAn provide microbial functional profiling.
MTD Explorer: evaluated implementation: Retains these methods in an updated, coordinated execution environment.
Interpretation and scope: Updated execution does not establish invention of functional profiling or increased annotation accuracy.

Original MTD: inspected baseline: DESeq2, ANCOM-BC and MaAsLin2 are incorporated.
MTD Explorer: evaluated implementation: Retains these methods with updated execution and reference-compatible handling.
Interpretation and scope: Statistical methods retain their original authorship; implementation changes require version-specific descriptions.

Original MTD: inspected baseline: The original R workflow includes a transcriptome_size covariate.
MTD Explorer: evaluated implementation: Retains the concept with explicit preparation and model handling.
Interpretation and scope: Transcriptome-size adjustment is inherited from the original MTD workflow.

Original MTD: inspected baseline: Composition, diversity, ordination and heatmaps are already produced.
MTD Explorer: evaluated implementation: Coordinates an expanded descriptive layer that also runs during group-comparison analyses.
Interpretation and scope: Exploratory graphics are shared outputs, not exclusive to the no-comparison route; the methods are inherited.

Original MTD: inspected baseline: No corresponding exploratory/no-comparison switch was identified in the examined entry points.
MTD Explorer: evaluated implementation: Provides an explicit route that retains descriptive outputs and omits contrast-dependent modules.
Interpretation and scope: The implementation is documented; the present reference run used comparisons and does not validate this route end to end.

Original MTD: inspected baseline: No corresponding composite score and ranking were identified in the examined baseline files.
MTD Explorer: evaluated implementation: Computes a weighted descriptive score, full rankings, component contributions, lollipop and landscape views.
Interpretation and scope: The score is a developer-defined heuristic, not a trained estimate or validated measure of biological importance; mean and total are dependent.

Original MTD: inspected baseline: Contaminant-read extraction is present; an equivalent ranking-driven extraction route was not identified.
MTD Explorer: evaluated implementation: Optionally extracts reads for ranked detected taxa, with top-N selection and mate validation.
Interpretation and scope: The benchmark used top-five extraction; this is distinct from the number of taxa displayed or statistically tested.

Original MTD: inspected baseline: Customized_host.sh accepts genome/GTF/TaxID and builds classification/alignment resources.
MTD Explorer: evaluated implementation: Coordinates genome, GTF and proteins, including downstream functional resources.
Interpretation and scope: The original already supported custom hosts; the extension concerns coordinated resources and functional infrastructure.

Original MTD: inspected baseline: The pinned registry contains 199 host rows, with 14 named OrgDb packages.
MTD Explorer: evaluated implementation: Records sources, assemblies, releases and resource links for coordinated reference handling.
Interpretation and scope: Original MTD already included a broad host registry; registry coverage is not an experimental validation count.

Original MTD: inspected baseline: The inspected enrichment route expects an existing named OrgDb; custom-reference construction does not create one.
MTD Explorer: evaluated implementation: Builds a compatible OrgDb when needed from reference IDs, representative proteins and eggNOG annotations using AnnotationForge.
Interpretation and scope: Uses the external AnnotationForge, AnnotationDbi and eggNOG-mapper methods. Compatibility and sufficient annotation are prerequisites; generated annotations are predictions.

Feature or capability: Reference- and expression-matched GO gene sets
Original MTD: inspected baseline: ssGSEA is included, but this reference-derived GMT construction was not identified in the examined route.
MTD Explorer: evaluated implementation: Creates a reference GO master GMT and filters gene sets against the expression input.
Interpretation and scope: This extends gene-set preparation, not the ssGSEA method; prepared and scoring-eligible set counts differ.

Original MTD: inspected baseline: OrgDb-based identifier conversion supports downstream KEGG analyses.
MTD Explorer: evaluated implementation: Adds an NCBI-based, provenance-recorded route retaining only unambiguous reference-ID mappings.
Interpretation and scope: The route maps existing identifiers and does not manufacture Entrez genes or remove organism-specific KEGG requirements.

Original MTD: inspected baseline: clusterProfiler/GSEA and functional visualizations are already included.
MTD Explorer: evaluated implementation: Extends reference-compatible annotation, naming, visual summaries and alternative mapping routes.
Interpretation and scope: Official KEGG organism maps and eggNOG-derived KO/pathway annotations are separate resources.

Original MTD: inspected baseline: Volcano plots are present, including an inspected ggplot-based implementation.
MTD Explorer: evaluated implementation: Integrates EnhancedVolcano for host and microbial comparison outputs.
Interpretation and scope: Uses the external EnhancedVolcano package; volcano plots and the package predate their integration into Explorer.

Original MTD: inspected baseline: HAllA is part of the original integration workflow.
MTD Explorer: evaluated implementation: Retains HAllA and supplies an optimized vectorized Spearman path and coordinated reports.
Interpretation and scope: The measured fast path used asymptotic Spearman p values despite a generic permutation setting; association is not causality.

Original MTD: inspected baseline: Equivalent input-identity/stage-validation mechanisms were not identified in the examined entry points.
MTD Explorer: evaluated implementation: Records input SHA-256 identities, parameters and local/HPC stage completion state.
Interpretation and scope: Checkpoint creation was observed; interruption recovery, runtime gain and fully cold-cache execution were not demonstrated.

Original MTD: inspected baseline: The publication includes HPC parallelism for ssGSEA; README describes interactive execution with Screen.
MTD Explorer: evaluated implementation: Adds Slurm task distribution, sample/chunk handling and task-level records/recovery.
Interpretation and scope: This is a specific new backend, not the first HPC use; local benchmark timings do not establish Slurm scaling.

Original MTD: inspected baseline: Conda-based installation, database updates and resumable downloads are present.
MTD Explorer: evaluated implementation: Reworks dedicated environments, validation and persistent/offline resource handling.
Interpretation and scope: Conda and resumable downloads are inherited capabilities; installation and robustness gains were not measured.
